summary: Rollout token rotation breaks session affinity causing unexpected model fallback
description:
Issue summary: During a staged rollout of redwood-7b-v3 -> redwood-7b-v3-quant, session tokens issued immediately prior to the control plane's token rotation lost affinity. A small cohort of BrightPathHealth production requests were routed to fallback model variants, causing degraded quality and increased token spend.

Impact: ~0.8% of requests for the customer in us-east saw model fallback to quantized variant for up to 90s per session. Customers reported increased hallucination rates and a spike in per-request token cost. BrightPathHealth flagged as P1 due to clinical workflow impact.

Environment: Production (dedicated pool) in us-east region. Dedicated capacity, tenant-specific routing with session-pin enabled. Rollout policy: weighted progressive promote (10% -> 30% -> 60%). Control plane performed scheduled token rotation at 2026-03-12T14:03:00Z during the 10% -> 30% weight window.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a session (client receives session token T_old).
2) Trigger a weighted promote (promote 7b-v3 to 7b-v3-quant).
3) Control plane executes token rotation for routing keys (T_new issued).
4) In-flight requests using T_old temporarily lose lookup in the affinity store and are routed to fallback path.

Observed behavior: Affinity lookup for session tokens issued before the rotation returned a cache miss for ~60-120s, after which affinity reconciled. During the miss window, the routing layer selected the cheaper compatible model variant (quant) rather than honoring the pinned version. Logs show affinity misses coincident with control plane rotation events and prefix cache invalidations.

Expected behavior: Token rotation should be transparent to in-flight sessions. Existing tokens should map to the pinned version until session TTL or explicit unpin. No routing fallback should occur for pinned sessions.

Preliminary logs/traces (snippets):
- routing-service[2026-03-12T14:03:01Z] WARN affinity_lookup.go:142 missing affinity for token="T_old_abc123" route_id=brightpath-health-prod
- router[2026-03-12T14:03:02Z] INFO fallback_decision.go:87 selected_variant=redwood-7b-v3-quant reason=affinity_miss
- gateway[2026-03-12T14:03:05Z] ERROR proxy.go:212 upstream_call=failed status=200->quality_drop

Root cause hypothesis: Token rotation updated the control-plane token->affinity mapping and triggered a short-lived eviction cascade in the distributed affinity cache (Redis cluster + local in-process shards). Local shards remained stale until background reconcilers repopulated entries. During that window, routing falls back to variant selection logic which prefers capacity-compatible models. Two contributing factors identified: (1) the token rotation procedure cleared TTLs on the affinity namespace before repopulation, and (2) the routing fallback logic treats affinity miss as equivalent to "no pin" rather than transient cache miss.

Mitigation / Workaround applied:
- Immediately toggled token rotation to deferred mode for the active rollout (control plane) to stop further rotation operations.
- Temporary change deployed to routing-service to treat affinity misses during a known rotation window as "hold current route" for 120s (hotfix).
- Notified BrightPathHealth SREs and opened a dedicated Slack channel #support-brightpathhealth to coordinate.

Current status: Hotfix (routing-service) deployed to prod-us-east at 2026-03-12T15:10:00Z which reduces observed fallback to ~0.05% of requests. Control plane patch to perform rotation-safe handoff is under review.

Next steps / action items:
- [Eng] Convert token rotation flow to multi-phase commit: pre-warm affinity keys in new namespace and atomically flip pointer (owner: Rohan Patel, PR in review).
- [SRE] Add monitoring alert for affinity-miss spike during rotations (owner: Elena Kovacs).
- [Product] Schedule coordinated maintenance windows for rotations with affected dedicated customers (owner: Priya Nambiar).
- [CS] Follow up with BrightPathHealth with post-incident summary and SLA credit proposal (owner: Maya Chen).

Follow-up: We plan a full postmortem if customer impact persists beyond the SLA window. Temporary rollback of rotation is in-flight until the two-phase rotation is validated in staging.
